object_description: two functionally separate bodies rising from a single-storey link, five storeys and a lower parallel part
geometry_property: uniform grid facade of precast concrete
design_condition: the volume sits at the street corner taking over the building lines of the neighbouring garage and sports hall, with the taller body along one street and the lower one parallel at the hall

positive: The volume takes over the building lines of the central garage and sports hall
The higher five-storey part stands along the street with the lower part parallel at the sports hall
A uniform grid-like facade of prefabricated concrete elements spans the entire building
The vertical slanted concrete elements are iridescent
Organising the two uses in two functionally independent parts seems plausible
Both parts are well structured with consistently separated entrances and vertical accesses
The parking garage and additional rooms are reached via the existing ramp
The reading room and library are clearly visible from outside
The work and ancillary rooms are efficiently arranged with the unexposed magazines above
The re-establishment process of the vehicle hall is practical
The roof area between the two bodies acts as an outdoor terrace
The structural errors could be corrected without significantly changing the project
Construction costs are in the middle range of the projects examined
negative: The body sits rather close to the central garage and leaves an unclear distance to the sports hall
The closed ground floor facade hardly meets the demands of publicity in urban space
The pergola-like continuation forms a fragile visual elevation not doing justice to the facade theme
The pictorial connotation of the uses with the protected buildings is not entirely convincing
The delivery beside the narrow ambulance entrance suggests a disruption
The manoeuvring distance at the vehicle hall remains minimal
The hoped-for lighting of the deep vehicle hall is not planned
Two further floors above the entrance are not considered useful
The roof terrace does not impress with the adjacent rooms of the two uses
Prefabricated ribbed ceiling elements have an unclear load-bearing direction without obvious joists
The pane effect of the ceilings is questionable and sound insulation and fire resistance would need proof
The installations in the rib level would have to be cross-connected under the ceiling
Unclear supporting structures leave out a clear statement about economic efficiency
